purpose: Implement the deterministic Emberfall v0.2 board domain core: 7x7 board, orthogonal connected-group Tap/Pop, Prism/Ash/Stone resolution, vertical-only gravity, sealed-column behavior and Wall pressure. This packet prepares the first gameplay implementation increment; it does not authorize execution before the baseline gate is accepted.
sources: EFB-000 baseline dependency: PR #4 accepted merge commit, after independent review of the current head and matching E00 evidence
EFB-001 rules dependency: PR #5 accepted merge commit containing Product Owner resolutions
constraints: Execution status is BLOCKED until independent review accepts the current PR #4 head with matching successful E00 workflow evidence and PR #5 Product Owner resolutions are accepted.
Use an isolated implementation branch from the accepted v0.2 handoff baseline; do not modify the legacy prototype branch.
The only live player board action is connected-group Tap/Pop. Do not implement or route live combat through SwapCells or match-3 line matching.
Board is 7x7 with orthogonal connectivity and minimum legal pop size 2; one hidden incoming row is maintained separately.
Gravity is vertical only; no horizontal column slide.
Initial visible topology follows ADR-002: rows 0-1 empty and rows 2-6 seeded, with deterministic deck-weighted sampling and explicit fallback telemetry.
Prism resolution follows ADR-004 and never merges two different base hues.
Ash Pop follows ADR-006: n-1 chip, zero base Ink.
Stone breaks follow ADR-007: one pre-removal snapshot batch; no recursive chain in the same pop.
Seal follows ADR-012 frozen-column semantics; sealed cells are excluded from player effects, gravity and Wall insertion for the duration.
Wall/Overflow follows ADR-008 exactly, including the explicitly adopted one-Flask penalty.
Keep the domain module pure Kotlin/JVM with no Android or Compose imports.
All state transitions are deterministic for seed + rules version + command log; use explicit RNG streams and transactional rejection.
No cards, full combat, progression, meta systems, monetization or content expansion in this increment.
No unapproved merge, publish or deploy; no secrets in commits or logs.
risks: R1: legacy SwapCells paths may remain reachable through ViewModel/navigation unless removed or isolated at the command boundary.
R1: Prism direct selection and mixed-adjacency tie-breaks can produce nondeterministic group membership if ordering is implicit.
R1: Seal and Wall rise can create irregular per-column movement if frozen-column rules are not modeled explicitly.
R1: board generation fallback can bias hue distribution if it silently repairs local cells.
R1: replay divergence can occur if board, enemy and card RNG streams are coupled or advanced inconsistently.
acceptance: Board domain model has explicit 7x7 coordinates, one incoming row and sealed-column state.
Tap selection computes one deterministic orthogonal group and rejects groups smaller than 2.
Prism direct Tap and Prism adjacency follow ADR-004 golden cases; no cross-hue bridge is possible.
Ash, Stone, Brand, gravity, Seal, Wall rise and Overflow are independently testable pure functions.
Gravity preserves relative order within each unsealed column and never moves horizontally.
Overflow produces the exact ADR-008 state transition, including damage, Flask, row burn, skipped shift and incoming-row retention.
Rejected commands are transactional and leave the committed board/RNG state unchanged.
Seed + deck + rules version reproduces byte-identical initial board and action replay.
Property tests cover coordinate bounds, no duplicate cells, group connectivity, gravity conservation, sealed-column invariants and save/replay.
Statistical test over at least 100,000 seeds validates deck-derived hue weights and records fallback frequency.
Pure-JVM boundary check passes; unit/property/golden tests, formatting, lint and build pass.
Independent Mastery review examines exact candidate SHA and test artifacts.
next_increment: After EFB-002 is accepted, EFB-003 implements turn phases, Ink resources, enemy intents and transactional effect queue; EFB-005 content expansion remains behind the board/combat vertical slice.
